headline: Warm Outdoor Pools for Cold British Winters

sentences.text: In Britain, many people like to swim outside.
But the winter is cold and the water is cold too.
Some outdoor pools have warm water all year.
One pool in Scotland is next to a long lake and has a sauna.
Another old pool in Bristol was fixed and opened again.
Outdoor swimming is popular in Britain, even when the weather is cold.
A new travel guide lists ten outdoor pools with heated water.
They are called lidos, and some of them are open all year.
One pool in Scotland looks out over a long sea lake and has a sauna next to it.
In Bristol, an old pool from the Victorian age was repaired and is open again.
The guide says a warm swim outside is a nice way to enjoy winter.
Open-air swimming is a British tradition, but winter water can be painfully cold.
A new guide has picked ten lidos, or outdoor pools, where the water is heated all year round.
In Scotland, one pool sits on the shore of Loch Fyne and includes an infinity pool with a sauna.
In Bristol, a Victorian pool has been carefully restored and welcomes swimmers again.
The other pools on the list are spread across the country, from small towns to big cities.
Many of them are run by local communities that saved the pools from closing.
The guide suggests that a warm swim in the open air is one of the best ways to brighten a grey winter day.
Outdoor swimming has become one of Britain's favorite pastimes, but anyone who has braved a lido in January knows how bitter the water can be.
A new travel guide offers a gentler option: ten heated outdoor pools that stay open throughout the winter.
Among them is a pool on the west coast of Scotland, set on the banks of Loch Fyne, where an infinity pool and sauna overlook the water.
In Bristol, a Victorian lido that was once left to decay has been restored and now draws swimmers year round.
The remaining pools are scattered across the country, from seaside towns to city parks.
Several were rescued from closure by local campaigners and are now managed by community groups.
The guide argues that a warm outdoor swim offers the pleasures of wild swimming without the shock of icy water.
For many readers, it may be the perfect excuse to pack a towel this winter.
Open-air swimming has blossomed into one of Britain's most cherished pastimes, yet anyone who has plunged into a lido in January can testify to how punishing the water becomes.
A new travel guide proposes a more forgiving alternative: ten heated outdoor pools that remain open throughout the winter months.
They include a spa on the west coast of Scotland, perched on the banks of Loch Fyne, where an infinity pool and sauna gaze out across the water.
In Bristol, a Victorian lido once abandoned to neglect has been painstakingly restored and now attracts swimmers all year round.
The remaining entries are dotted across the country, from seaside resorts to leafy city parks.
Several were snatched from closure by determined local campaigners and are today run by community organizations.
The guide contends that a warm open-air swim delivers the exhilaration of wild swimming without the jolt of icy water.
For many readers, it may prove the perfect pretext for packing a towel this winter.
